subject: Request: executive endorsement for SpeedGuard pilot SLA carveout
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@speedguard.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot proposal + temporary SLA adjustment request

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion, SpeedGuard wants to run a 90-day pilot for threat-detection features that will hit our streaming inference path. To keep the pilot cost-effective for you, we're proposing a limited SLA adjustment for the pilot period and a short commercial concession. High-level proposal: 

- Pilot length: 90 days starting on deployment date
- Temporary uptime target for pilot: 99.5% (vs our standard 99.95%)
- Service credit: capped at 30% of monthly pilot fees, applied on a rolling monthly basis if uptime below threshold
- Commercial: 20% off list pricing for pilot months (incentive to run pilot)
- Conditions: telemetry access for performance tuning; deployment in us-west region only; standard security add-ons to be completed before go-live

I've attached a short Mutual Action Plan and a redline-ready terms doc for the deal desk to review (attachment: pilot-mop.pdf). If you can confirm you agree in principle, I'll loop in our deal desk and legal to get exec signoff.

Next steps: please confirm pilot start target (we suggested July 6) and any non-negotiables on your side.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai

Attachment: pilot-mop.pdf (1 page)
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@speedguard.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot proposal + temporary SLA adjustment request

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few points from our side before you escalate: 

- The features in scope are customer-facing for our enterprise fleet; 99.5% feels low for production-equivalent testing. Can we limit the concession to non-critical endpoints only?
- Service credit cap is workable, but we need guaranteed incident response times for severity 1s during pilot hours.
- Commercial: the 20% pilot discount is important to our procurement team; they will not sign unless it appears in the MSA appendix.

If you can get a short exec endorsement that this exception is strictly timeboxed to the pilot and that production will revert to standard SLA, procurement will push this through faster. Also need to see your redline (proposed-terms-redline.docx) so we can route internally.

Thanks —
Lisa Chen
Head of Partnerships | SpeedGuard Inc.
lisa@speedguard.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot proposal + temporary SLA adjustment request — request for deal desk + exec review

Marissa / Vivek —

Looping you both for deal desk / exec endorsement. Customer (SpeedGuard) is willing to pilot but insists on the commercial discount and firm service credit language. They specifically want a timeboxed exception that shows up in the MSA appendix. Key ask: can we approve a 90-day exception to reduce the uptime target to 99.5% for the pilot and provide a capped service credit + pilot discount? Risks: potential precedent setting; we must ensure rollback to standard SLA for prod. 

Proposed internal guardrails (my recommendation):
- Approval scope: pilot only (90 days) and only for endpoints labeled "experimental" in the MAP
- Uptime target: 99.5% for pilot months only
- Service credit: capped at 30% of monthly pilot fees, payable only after engineering verification of incident impact (to avoid spurious claims)
- Discount: 15% (reduced from customer request of 20%) — preserves margin while providing incentive
- Must include A/B fallback (smaller model) and agreed telemetry shippers for perf visibility

Attaching the customer's redline and my suggested redline (proposed-terms-redline.docx). Lauren — any legal must-haves I missed? Marissa / Vivek — need a quick exec decision to keep the July 6 target.

Thanks,
Jordan

Attachment: proposed-terms-redline.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Pilot proposal + temporary SLA adjustment request — request for deal desk + exec review

Jordan —

I read the attached redline. Commercially, I support a controlled pilot concession to win momentum with SpeedGuard but recommend we tighten caps and add explicit end-of-pilot re-evaluation language. Specifics I'd approve to send upward: 

- Pilot duration: 90 days, non-extendable without exec re-approval
- Pilot uptime: 99.5%
- Service credit: cap at 25% of monthly pilot fees (reduced from 30%) and require post-incident RCA before payout
- Discount: 15% for pilot months only; no legacy discount beyond pilot
- Non-production scope: limit to endpoints flagged in MAP and to the us-west region

Lauren — legal asks that we include: 1) explicit rollback clause stating production will revert to standard SLA; 2) telemetry/data access limited to perf metadata (no raw customer data); 3) acceptance criteria for the pilot (uptime/latency thresholds and verification method).

If Vivek is comfortable with these constraints, please sign off and we'll send a short exec endorsement email that we can append to the MSA.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Exec endorsement: SpeedGuard pilot SLA carveout (SG-4421)

Team —

I've reviewed the recommendation and the customer's ask. Executive endorsement granted with the following final conditions (non-negotiable):

1) Timebox: Pilot runs for 90 days from go-live; any extension requires written sign-off from me (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai).
2) Uptime: Temporary pilot uptime target set at 99.5% only for endpoints explicitly listed in the MAP; all other endpoints remain at standard SLA.
3) Credits: Service credit capped at 25% of monthly pilot fees, payable only after a verified RCA and confirmation from our incident review board.
4) Discount: Pilot pricing discount approved at 15% for pilot months; no permanent price change.
5) Safeguards: Customer must enable our telemetry exporters (performance-only) and accept a pre-launch security checklist. If security review fails, exception is void.
6) Operational fallback: We require an agreed fallback (smaller model or degraded feature flag) to reduce customer impact for identified SLO risk patterns.

Jordan: email the customer the exec endorsement and updated appendix language. Keep legal (Lauren) and deal desk (Marissa) on the thread; I'll monitor. Good to proceed if SpeedGuard accepts.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer (on behalf of Exec Committee) | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
